summary: Verified as a pure move by measurement, not by reading. AckOrderTest.java is byte-identical to HEAD after undoing the Invariants.->AckOrderInvariants. rename (diff of the normalised files is empty), so no assertion was weakened, reworded or deleted and all 14 @Test methods survive. The moved 96-line region (AckEvent + checkAckOrder) is byte-identical to the deleted region modulo indentation, the dropped 'public' modifiers and one javadoc link requalification. 12 mutations applied to AckOrderInvariants.checkAckOrder in its NEW home, each run against AckOrderTest: 10 killed, covering the three behaviours the task named -- base-from-lowest-observed (Math::min->Math::max KILLED; base shared across epochs KILLED; confirm-path base forced to 0 KILLED), the watermark (while->if KILLED; watermark map shared across epochs KILLED; confirmations not recorded KILLED), and per-epoch chain identity (confirmed set shared across epochs KILLED). Also killed: return List.of(), own-write-unconfirmed arm removed, ack/confirm branch negated. The 2 survivors are EQUIVALENT mutants, not test gaps: (1) the ack-path lazy base 'k -> base.get(k)' is only evaluated when the epoch has no prior confirmed event, in which case 'seen' is empty and the !seen.contains arm fires first, so w is never read -- forcing it to 0 cannot change any output; (2) 'w < e.sequence()' -> 'w <= e.sequence()' is reachable only in the else of !seen.contains, and the confirm path maintains the invariant w NOT-IN seen, so w == e.sequence() is unreachable there. Both survive identically against the pre-move code, since the code is byte-identical. Full :sequencer suite green in the review tree. Nothing else in the tree referenced Invariants.checkAckOrder or Invariants.AckEvent (grep over all *.java): the only remaining mentions are javadoc @links in Invariants.java, which the diff repointed.
